questions.q: What does RPO (Recovery Point Objective) measure, per this lesson?
options: How much recent data can be lost — the acceptable gap between protection points
How long the recovery process itself is allowed to take
The number of subscribers in a replication topology
The uptime percentage guaranteed by an SLA
questions.explain: RPO is about acceptable data loss, expressed as a time gap between protection points like backups or replication events.

questions.q: What does RTO (Recovery Time Objective) measure?
options: How much downtime is acceptable — the speed of the recovery process itself
How much data can be lost during a failure
The frequency of full backups
The size of the transaction log
questions.explain: RTO is about acceptable downtime — how quickly the system must be back online and usable.

questions.q: What does a tight RPO (near-zero) require, per this lesson?
options: Synchronous replication (e.g. a synchronous AG or database mirroring) so a transaction isn't committed until hardened at the secondary
A nightly full backup is always sufficient
SIMPLE recovery model is preferred for a tight RPO
RPO has no relationship to any specific technology
questions.explain: A near-zero RPO requires continuous, synchronous protection of every committed transaction, not periodic backups alone.

questions.q: What does a tight RTO (minutes or automatic) require, per this lesson?
options: A technology that fails over automatically or with minimal manual intervention, like an AG with a listener or an FCI
A slower, fully manual restore process is acceptable
RTO is always satisfied automatically regardless of technology
Tight RTO requires disabling all backups
questions.explain: A tight RTO needs fast, largely automatic recovery — manual restore processes are too slow to meet it.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what's the realistic failure mode around RPO/RTO in practice?
options: The business is never actually asked for these targets, so IT guesses or defaults to whatever technology is already in place
Businesses always demand RPO and RTO of zero regardless of cost
RPO and RTO must always be identical for every system
RPO/RTO targets are set automatically by SQL Server
questions.explain: The lesson stresses that the real DBA job is translating an actual business conversation about acceptable loss/downtime into technology — not guessing without asking.
